::: {#exr-daisy-blow-kitchen}
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| label: C15-dzdau
f <- doodle_fun(~ x & y, seed = 93822)
set.seed(101)
Pts <- tibble::tibble(
  y = runif(5, -3.5, 3.5),
  x = runif(5, -3.5, 3.5),
  labels = LETTERS[5:1]
)
contour_plot(f(x, y) ~ x & y, domain(x = -4:4, y = -4:4)) |>
  gf_text(y ~ x, label = ~ labels, data = Pts, 
          size = 6, color = "black", inherit = FALSE) |>
  gf_refine(coord_fixed()) |>
  gf_theme(theme_minimal())
  

```


Here is a contour plot of a function $f(x, y)$, annotated with several letters. At each of the letters, say what is the direction of the gradient vector. As names for directions, we will use the eight major compass points: N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW. Choose Zero if the gradient vector is so short that the direction is essentially meaningless.

`r choices <- c("N", "NE", "E", "SE", "S", "SW", "W", "NW", "Zero")`

1. At point A: `r devoirs::devoirs_set(choices, correct = "NW", n = 9, id = "dbk-A-dkws")`

2. At point B: `r devoirs::devoirs_set(choices, correct = "SW", n = 9, id = "dbk-B-dkws")`

3. At point C: `r devoirs::devoirs_set(choices, correct = "S", n = 9, id = "dbk-C-dkws")`

4. At point D: `r devoirs::devoirs_set(choices, correct = "NW", n = 9, id = "dbk-D-dkws")`

5. At point E: `r devoirs::devoirs_set(choices, correct = "Zero", n = 9, id = "dbk-E-dkws")`

:::
